correctness.rationale: The normalized Poincare map Q is analytic near the harmonic orbit; when the two odd terms vanish, the surviving even-power field is reversible under (X,Y)->(-X,Y), so its entire local return is exactly the identity. First energy variations give the negative beta-moment derivatives in the two odd coefficients, with remainder divisible by their total magnitude. After delta scaling, the return has uniform C1 expansion identity+delta^(2n)G+o(delta^(2n)). Discrete Gronwall on compact trajectories proves the finite slow-time flow limit. Sign crossing near the unique positive zero and the derivative Gprime<0 yield the small attracting cycle and its multiplier; the cited source supplies global uniqueness. At zero coefficient the local return is r-I_n r^(2n+1)+o(r^(2n+1)), and telescoping r_k^(-2n) proves the critical law. Exact trigonometric coefficients were independently recomputed, and numerical return checks pass. Limitations are local in amplitude and finite in slow time.

value.rationale: The initiating uniqueness theorem does not quantify the singular loss of hyperbolicity or timescale of convergence. The result supplies the entire limiting transient (a nonlinear ODE, not just an arbitrary coefficient), a sharp selected cycle-radius constant, a precise Floquet multiplier deficit, and matching algebraic critical slowdown, all for a natural multi-exponent family with a nonzero reversible even perturbation. The reversible cancellation explains why the even coefficient does not modify the leading transition, a useful structural fact in degenerate bifurcation analysis. No claim of universal error rate or global basin is made.
